title: A row cell note counts toward the row's height
body: A `note` under a row cell draws below the cell, but neither the cell's height nor the space a `stack` gives the row counts it. In `figures/sufr-build.acre` the rank table needed a spacer box under it, and the merge rows of section 9 gave every cell a blank note so their numbers line up. The proposal is that a row with notes is as tall as its tallest note reaches.
close_reason: Landed in 0d8260b. A note sat inside its cell at 0.78 of the height, not below it, and only a note too large for the unit spilled out. `row::height` now raises a row's unit height until its tallest note fits, so a stack, a brace and an arrow use the taller row. `Row::noted` puts every text of a row with a note at 0.4 of the height, so a cell needs no blank note to line up with its neighbours. Rows without notes still centre their text, so the blank notes in the one-cell merge rows of `figures/sufr-build.acre` still line those rows up with the rows above them. No existing figure renders differently.
